items.title: Section: Skilfully Converting a Miser — "Borrow From My House, You Will Lose Nothing"

items.zh: 菩薩即便往詣其舍，慰問安不？恭順方便，告言：汝來，我不令汝庫藏減盡，而於現前作大饒益。我家現有廣多財寶、廣多施物，為滿我施波羅蜜多，若有求者來到汝所，勿令空返，可至我家取諸財寶，隨意施與。或有求者來至我所，我行施時，汝於此施當生隨喜。
items.en: The bodhisattva goes directly to that household, offers a warm greeting, and, with respectful, skilful tact, says: come, I will not let your own storehouse diminish in the least, while still accomplishing something of great benefit right now. My own household has abundant wealth and abundant gifts ready to give — to help complete my own perfection of giving, should anyone come seeking help at your door, do not let them leave empty-handed; simply send them to my house to take whatever wealth they need, freely. ... Or should someone come to me instead while I am giving, you are welcome to rejoice together in that very act of giving.

items.zh: 彼聞是已，便生欣悅：於我庫藏既無所減，復得稱彼善男子心，故應隨順成辦所作。菩薩如是令彼漸種當來調伏慳悋種子，由慧為先善巧方便，令漸修習自捨少財，依下無貪進得中品，依中無貪進得上品。
items.en: Hearing this, the miser feels genuine delight: since their own storehouse suffers no loss at all, and this also fulfils the wish of that good bodhisattva, they willingly go along and carry it out. In this way, the bodhisattva plants, little by little, the seed that will eventually tame the miser's own stinginess — through wisdom-guided skilful means, gradually leading them to give away a small amount of their own wealth, progressing from a lesser degree of non-greed to a middling degree, and from a middling degree to a genuinely great one.

items.title: Section: Helping Fellow Renunciants Give, and Never Exposing a Petitioner's Deception

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若親教師及軌範師、共住弟子同梵行者，性是慳貪，是慳貪類；或性雖非慳貪種類，而闕資財，所欲匱乏。菩薩欲寄佛法僧田樹修布施福業事時，捨所施物與彼令作，已自不為。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, if their own preceptor, instructing teacher, resident disciple, or fellow renunciant is by nature stingy, or is not stingy by nature but genuinely lacks the means, when wishing to cultivate the merit of giving towards the field of the three jewels, give them the object to be offered and let them personally carry out the act, rather than doing it themselves.

items.zh: 菩薩如是巧慧方便，自所生福彌更弘多。復令一類同梵行者，調伏所有慳貪煩惱，亦令一類樂善法者，所願滿足，攝受有情、成熟有情。又諸菩薩現有眾多可施財物，見諸來者有希求相，知其心已，隨彼所樂悉皆施與。
復有商人為性矯詐，欲行欺誑，菩薩知已，尚掩其過不令他知，況觸於彼。稱滿其願，令無羞愧，踊躍無畏，歡喜而去。復有矯詐欺誑，菩薩初不覺知，後時乃覺；雖復覺知，不以此事舉發彼人，亦不訶責為作憶念。但生悲愍：彼於我所誤行如是不與取事，我今隨喜，令彼無罪。
items.en: Should a merchant, deceitful by nature, attempt to swindle the bodhisattva, the bodhisattva, aware of this, still conceals the person's fault rather than exposing it, let alone confronting them — fulfilling their wish so completely that they feel no shame, leaving joyfully and without fear. And should someone deceive the bodhisattva in a way not noticed until later, even once recognised, the bodhisattva does not expose or reprimand them for it, but simply feels compassion: this person has mistakenly taken what was not given from me; I now rejoice in it, so that they incur no fault.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為菩薩現有可施財物巧慧而施。

items.title: Section: Giving With No Material Wealth at All — Four Methods

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若現無有可施財物，先所串習彼彼世間工巧業處作意現前，少用功力，多集財寶，施諸眾生。是諸菩薩，或復為他種種美妙、善巧言詞宣說正法，令貧苦者尚樂行施，況富樂者；令慳貪者猶能惠施，況習施者。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, if presently without any material object to give, bring to mind some previously mastered worldly craft, and with little effort gather wealth to give to beings. Bodhisattvas also teach the true dharma to others in language both doctrinally sound and skilfully expressed, moving even the poor and suffering to delight in giving, how much more so the wealthy and comfortable; moving even the stingy to give, how much more so those already accustomed to it.

items.zh: 或有淨信多饒財寶常樂施家，數教乞者往彼求索，令其布施。或彼惠捨修福業時，躬詣其所，翹勤無惰，起策具足，深心歡喜，隨力隨能身助、語助，令施求者得善滿足。以彼施時，事力闕尠，或惡供瞻，或墮朋黨，或不恭敬，或念忘失，由善助故，斯過皆無。
items.en: Or, knowing a household of genuine faith, abundant wealth, and constant delight in giving, one repeatedly directs petitioners there to ask, so that household can give. Or, when another is carrying out an act of giving as their own merit, one personally attends, tirelessly diligent, wholeheartedly joyful, helping with body and speech according to one's own ability, so that both giver and petitioner are genuinely satisfied — since, without such help, giving often suffers from insufficient hands, poor-quality offerings, favoritism towards some over others, careless or disrespectful handling, or a distracted, forgetful mind; through this skilful assistance, none of these faults arise.

items.zh: 如是菩薩現無財寶，巧慧方便而行布施，此說乃至未證增上清淨意樂。

items.title: Section: Ground-Level Bodhisattvas Never Lack Wealth, and Why Teaching the Dharma Surpasses Giving Material Things

items.zh: 若諸菩薩已證增上清淨意樂，如已獲得超諸惡趣，如是生生必定獲得無盡財寶。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who have already realised an elevated, purified intention — just as they have attained going beyond the miserable realms, so too, life after life, they are certain to obtain inexhaustible wealth.

items.title: Section: When Scripture Should Never Be Given — Guarding the Teaching From Misuse

items.zh: 又諸菩薩、終不口授求過外道所有正法，亦不施彼所寫經典；知性多貪，求欲衒賣經卷等者，亦不施與；知欲祕藏，亦不施與；不求勝智，亦不施與，必求勝智。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never orally teach the true dharma to an outsider seeking to find fault with it, nor give them a written copy of scripture. Knowing someone of greedy character seeks a scripture only to peddle it for profit, this too is not given. Knowing someone wishes only to hoard it away secretly, this too is not given. To one not genuinely seeking excellent wisdom, nothing is given — it is given only to one who genuinely does.

items.title: Section: A Scripture Already Mastered Is Given Freely — One Still Being Studied Is Read Like a Treasure First

items.zh: 若自了知於經卷等其義已辯，即隨所樂如應施與。若自了知於經卷等其義未辯，為辯義故恒自披轉。如是菩薩若見其餘有經卷等，即應方便轉求施與，或更書寫而施與之。
items.en: If bodhisattvas know that a scripture's meaning has already been mastered, they give it away as requested, freely. If they know its meaning is not yet mastered, and they still constantly study it in order to grasp that meaning, then, seeing that a fellow practitioner has another copy, they should skilfully arrange for that copy to be given instead, or personally produce a new copy to give.

items.title: Section: Honest Self-Examination Before Declining — Is It Stinginess, or Genuine Need?

items.zh: 若不見餘有經卷等，亦無力能更為書寫，即應審諦觀察自心：勿我於法慳垢纏心，不能施耶？勿我於法別意所礙，不欲施耶？為我於法有勝所須，不應施耶？
items.en: If no other copy can be found, and there is no ability to produce a new one, one should carefully examine one's own mind: is it that I am gripped by stinginess towards the teaching, and so cannot give it? Is it that some other affliction towards this person obstructs me, and so I do not wish to give it? Or is it that I have a genuine, excellent need for it, and so should not give it?

items.zh: 如是審諦觀察心已，若自了知，我於此法少有慳纏、別意所礙而不施者，即作是心：我今決定應行法施。設我由此行法施故，於現法中即成癡瘂，不忍煩惱尚應法施，況令闕乏妙智資糧。
items.en: Having carefully examined the mind in this way, if one recognises that stinginess or some other affliction is genuinely the obstacle preventing giving, one thinks: I should now decisively give the teaching. Even should giving the teaching leave me, in this present life, dull-witted and mute, giving it is still called for simply to overcome my own affliction — how much more so, then, when withholding it would leave my own provisions of excellent wisdom lacking in the first place.

blocks.text: Skilful ways of giving: helping misers become generous, giving without money, and the special case of giving the Dharma itself.

The bodhisattva visits a stingy household and says: "Come, I will not let your storehouse diminish in the least": I will provide the goods; you hand them out. "The miser feels genuine delight, since his storehouse suffers no loss." Master Cháng Bǎi: gradually the miser says, "next time I'll add some of my own".

If one's teacher or fellow monastic is stingy, or simply lacks means, and wishes to make an offering to the Three Jewels, one gives them the object to offer. If a merchant tries to cheat, "the bodhisattva, aware of it, still conceals the fault".

Four ways: using a craft to earn something to give; teaching the Dharma so skilfully that "even the poor and the stingy" are moved to give; directing petitioners to a generous household; and personally helping when someone else gives, "so that both giver and petitioner are satisfied", since without help giving often suffers from too few hands or careless handling. Master Cháng Bǎi: telling stories is one such skilful teaching.
Bodhisattvas of purified intention "are certain, life after life, to obtain inexhaustible wealth". And "teaching the Dharma surpasses giving material things".
Not to "an outsider seeking to find fault with it", nor to someone "who seeks a scripture only to peddle it". Venerable Miào Jìng: 衒 is walking about hawking it.

"If its meaning is already mastered, they give it freely. If not yet mastered", they study it first. Before declining, "examine one's own mind: is it stinginess towards the teaching?" If so, give it at once.

quiz.q: The bodhisattva gradually leads the miser "from a lesser degree of non-greed to a middling degree." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: the miser donates everything at once
the bodhisattva gives powdered milk; the miser gradually says "next time I'll give two cans," then "next time I'll give it all"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: gradually the miser says, "next time I'll put in two cans"; later, "next time I'll give it all" — progressing to the middling degree. Venerable Miào Jìng: first giving a small amount is the lesser degree of non-greed.

quiz.q: If one's preceptor or instructing teacher is stingy by nature or lacks means, what does the bodhisattva do when wishing to make merit towards the three jewels?
options: do it alone without telling them
give them the object and let them carry out the act, rather than doing it oneself
urge them to pay debts first
wait until they stop being stingy
quiz.why: "When wishing to cultivate the merit of giving towards the field of the three jewels, give them the object to be offered and let them personally carry out the act, rather than doing it themselves." Venerable Miào Jìng: the merit is greater than making the offering oneself.

quiz.q: If bodhisattvas presently have nothing material to give, what does the treatise say they can do?
options: recall a previously mastered worldly craft, and with little effort gather wealth to give to beings
quiz.why: "If presently without any material object to give, [they] bring to mind some previously mastered worldly craft, and with little effort gather wealth to give to beings." Master Cháng Bǎi: for example, writing one piece of calligraphy that sells for a million.

quiz.q: "Teaching the true dharma in language both doctrinally sound and skilfully expressed." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "skilfully expressed"?
options: teaching with skilful means, such as telling stories — some beings dislike hearing principles but enjoy stories
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: teaching through skilful means, such as telling stories, is what "skilful" means. Some beings dislike hearing principles but enjoy stories, so bodhisattvas use both approaches.

quiz.q: "Knowing someone of greedy character seeks a scripture only to 'xuàn-sell' it, this too is not given." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "xuàn"?
options: walking along and calling out — hawking the scripture
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "xuàn" means walking along calling out — hawking the scripture. Master Cháng Bǎi: someone who wants a scripture only to resell it is not given one, since they never read it. The English "sell or show it off" adds showing off, which Master Cháng Bǎi places under "not seeking excellent wisdom."

quiz.q: When a scripture's meaning is not yet mastered, the bodhisattva "constantly studies it." How do the two lectures explain this?
options: Miào Jìng: reading it again and again, or consulting reference works; Cháng Bǎi: "immersing and going back and forth" — steeping oneself in it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: reading it once and again, or looking for reference books to study. Master Cháng Bǎi: one must "immerse and go back and forth" — the way to read is to steep oneself in the text.

quiz.q: Having examined the mind, if one recognises that stinginess or another affliction is the obstacle, what does the bodhisattva think?
options: wait until the affliction is gone
I should now decisively give the teaching
don't give, to avoid more stinginess
quiz.why: "If one recognises that stinginess or some other affliction is genuinely the obstacle preventing giving, one thinks: I should now decisively give the teaching." Venerable Miào Jìng: if you are stingy with the dharma, you will later become dull and foolish, like Cūḍapanthaka.
